job.title: Assistant Director, Intelligence and Market Surveillance
job.description:
Applications must be made by attaching a completed application form via the Conscia website which can be downloaded below.


GRAI Application Form - Assistant Director, Intelligence & Market Surveillance (Assistant Principal Officer).docx

GRAI Candidate Booklet - Assistant Director, Intelligence and Market Surveillance (Assistant Principal Officer).pdf


Vacancy

The GRAI is seeking to appoint an Assistant Director, Intelligence and Market Surveillance (Assistant Principal Officer - Standard Scale). Successful applicants will be placed on a panel for a period of up to 18 months, from which GRAI may fill future vacancies for Assistant Director, Intelligence and Market Surveillance (Assistant Principal Officer - Standard Scale).


About the Role

You will lead the Authority’s data-driven enforcement strategy, ensuring evidence from OSINT, market monitoring, and protected disclosures is gathered and analysed to support risk-based regulatory decisions.


Key Responsibilities include:

  • Establish & Lead: Build the Intelligence & Market Surveillance Unit from the ground up, defining business requirements for secure ICT systems and digital evidence management.
  • Intelligence Oversight: Oversee the triage and analysis of intelligence from multiple sources, including partner agencies like An Garda Síochána and international counterpart organisations.
  • Market Monitoring: Monitor gambling markets and digital platforms to identify emerging risks, trends, and indicators of criminal activity or regulatory breaches.
  • Strategic Output: Produce high-quality intelligence products and briefings to inform enforcement strategy and operational decision-making.
  • Standards & Governance: Establish protocols for intelligence handling, classification, and retention in accordance with legal, evidential, and data protection requirements.
  • Team Development: Lead and mentor a high-performing team of investigators and enforcement staff, promoting best practices in information governance.
  • Collaboration: Maintain effective relationships with external stakeholders, including domestic regulators and law enforcement, to support cross-agency intelligence sharing.


Essential Criteria:

To be eligible to apply for this role you must have/demonstrate in your application form that you meet the following essential criteria:

  • A third-level degree (minimum Level 8 on the NFQ) in a relevant discipline such as law, data analytics, policing, forensic computing or a related field.
  • A minimum of 5 years’ experience in one or more of the following fields: intelligence analysis, market surveillance, regulatory enforcement, law-enforcement, including at least 3 years at a managerial level.
  • Proven expertise in intelligence lifecycle management, including ingestion, triage, analysis, dissemination and review.
  • Experience working with OSINT tools and digital-platform monitoring.
  • Experience in data analysis, risk assessment and production of intelligence products that support decision making.
  • Demonstrable experience in leading online investigations, including open source and covert investigations.
  • Demonstrable experience in digital evidence management.


A comprehensive candidate booklet containing the full job specification, essential and desirable criteria, and more, is available for download below.


GRAI Candidate Booklet - Assistant Director, Intelligence and Market Surveillance (Assistant Principal Officer).pdf

GRAI Application Form - Assistant Director, Intelligence & Market Surveillance (Assistant Principal Officer).docx

Conscia will be managing all aspects of the recruitment process on behalf of the Gambling Regulatory Authority of Ireland.


Applications must be made by attaching a completed application form via the Conscia website.


Only applications fully submitted online will be accepted into the campaign.


Applications will not be accepted after the closing date of Monday 9th November at 3pm

job.title: Assistant Executive Manager Finance (Grade II Accountant)
job.description:
Candidate Handbook Assistant Executive Manager Finance (1).pdf


SFPA Application Form - Assistant Executive Manager Finance (Grade II Accountant).docx


The Sea Fisheries Protection Authority is seeking an Assistant Executive Manager, Finance (Grade II Accountant).


This is a rewarding and challenging role for an individual who can demonstrate the ability to support and manage the financial operations of the Authority, ensuring effective financial planning, budget management, financial reporting and compliance with relevant financial regulations and policies.


Key Responsibilities include but are not limited to:


• Preparation of the annual statutory financial statements in accordance with FRS 102, the financial reporting standard applicable in the UK and Ireland issued by the Financial Reporting Council (FRC). 

• Preparation for the annual audit by the Comptroller and Auditor General (C&AG) and dealing with any issues arising.

• Providing expert advice across the unit on audit and financial management issues. 

• Lead Liaison with the internal and external auditors. 

• Oversee the operation of financial functions within the Finance unit. 

• Maintaining and enhancing the financial control environment, ensuring the accounting system, procedures and processes are in compliance with public financial procedures, best practice, and generally accepted accounting standards and principles. 

• Leading the completion of monthly management accounts and related reconciliations. 

• Oversight of the organisation’s Fixed Asset Register. 

• Ensuring compliance with taxation obligations. 

• Support the preparation of the annual Business Plan for the unit.


Essential Requirements:

• Have full membership of a prescribed accountancy body supervised by the Irish Auditing and Accounting Supervisory Authority (IAASA) 

• Minimum of 5 years relevant post qualification accountancy/audit experience including financial accounting and/or management accounting, financial 

services, fund management or the regulatory environment 

• A high degree of analytical, conceptual and problem-solving skills in financial and business management 

• A good understanding of public sector accounting and financial management systems 

• Experience of managing and supervising a team including performance management


Desirable Requirements:

• Practical experience operating within a public sector, civil service, or highly regulated environment, including familiarity with public spending codes and statutory reporting guidelines. 

• Proven experience preparing for or directly managing interactions with state audit bodies (such as the Comptroller and Auditor General), internal audit committees, or external regulators. 

• Prior experience supervising, mentoring, or coaching staff. 

• A track record of identifying operational inefficiencies and successfully implementing automated workflows or system-driven process improvements. 

• Basic User competence in the Irish language would be desirable


How to Apply:

Applications must be made by way of application form.

Completed application forms must be uploaded via this portal no later than 5pm (Irish time) on Thursday 5th November 2026.

job.title: Officer, Finance and Governance - Data Protection and Compliance
job.description:
﻿Key Details:

 

Location: Galway or Kerry

Contract: Temporary, Specified Purpose Contract, Full-time (Approximate end date September 2027)*

*The specific purpose of this contract is to cover a temporary internal move.

Salary: €58,528 – €83,697 (starting at the first point of the scale)

Closing date: Monday, 2 November 2026 at 3pm


Application Form: Failte Ireland_Officer, Finance and Governance - Data Protection and Compliance _Temp_Application Form.docx


Job Purpose: 


The Officer, Finance and Governance - Data Protection and Compliance supports the effective delivery of data protection and compliance management across Fáilte Ireland. The role contributes to personal data protection compliance by ensuring that appropriate technical and organisational measures are in place and effective, and that the organisation can demonstrate, monitor and report on compliance with the GDPR and the Irish Data Protection Acts. The role also plays a key role in strengthening Fáilte Ireland's compliance and governance framework through compliance monitoring, reporting and assurance activities, while promoting the consistent application of policies, procedures and regulatory obligations across the organisation. 


Job Description/ Key Areas of Responsability: 

  

Data Protection Compliance Management 

  • Act as the first point of contact for internal and external privacy queries. 
  • Ensure the appropriate technical and organisational measures are in place to ensure effective data protection governance and reporting including:


  • Risk identification and risk management (privacy by design & default)
  • Control management
  • KPI identification and reporting


  • Support colleagues and divisions, managing data protection service desk queries
  • Manage data protection governance documentation, supporting the Data Protection Officer (DPO) in relation to governance management and reporting.
  • Ensure Personal Data Requests and Data Breach procedures are effectively monitored, managed, responded to, logged and reported on.
  • Prepare submissions to the Data Protection Commission on behalf of the DPO where required and maintain all related logs.
  • Ensure Records of Processing Activities are well managed and kept up to date in line with Article 30 of the GDPR.
  • Actively manage the Privacy by Design and Default procedure
  • Conduct Data Protection Impact Assessments and Legitimate Interest Assessment
  • Work with teams across the organisation to reduce and remove risks from divisional GDPR risk registers.
  • Manage a programme of continuous development, identifying and addressing improvement opportunities.
  • Keep abreast of data protection legislation and guidance from the Data Protection Commission.


Compliance Management


  • Manage, monitor and track processes and procedures used to support organisational compliance with key areas of legislation, including compliance logs, policy and procedure updates and registers.
  • Manage the effective operation of outsourced legal services by establishing clear contact and escalation protocols, ensuring Fáilte Ireland staff can access the appropriate legal support and promptly addressing delayed responses or uncertainty about points of contact.
  • Work with teams across the organisation to ensure compliance with legislation including Official Languages Act and the Public Sector and Human Rights Duty
  • Work with teams across the organisation to reduce and remove compliance risks 
  • Ensure the maintenance and continuous improvement of Fáilte Ireland’s governance framework, ensuring that policies, procedures, are clearly documented, current and applied consistently.
  • Ensure compliance with all applicable public-sector governance requirements across Fáilte Ireland working in partnership with the Governance Team and relevant stakeholders

 

Reporting, Stakeholder Engagement and Programme Delivery


  • Produce senior management compliance reports for the DPO, Executive Team and Audit, Risk and Registration Committee.
  • Support effective staff training and develop training or briefing content on legislative compliance, including GDPR.
  • Manage external legal service provider contracts, ensuring effective ways of working, reporting arrangements and SLAs are in place.
  • Contract, budget and relationship management with the outsourced legal services provider
  • Manage and report on service quality and conduct annual reviews in a timely manner.
  • Manage budget and resources as required and ensure procurement and purchasing are in line with Fáilte Ireland policy.
  • Establish and maintain effective working relationships with internal colleagues across all teams.
  • Provide regular detailed reports to stakeholders, including the level and evaluation of work activity, and escalate high-risk issues as required.
  • Develop and deliver an annual plan of work
  • Work as part of project teams and manage projects as required. 
  • Comply with all aspects of organisation policy and promote good governance across the team.
  • Ensure procurement, expenditure and activities are managed in line with Fáilte Ireland policy, public spending obligations, public financial procedures, and delegated authority.
  • Ensure plans are delivered in line with agreed budgeted spend.


People Management


  • Manage all staff reporting to the position to effectively train, evaluate, motivate, delegate, and monitor their activities.


Carry out all other duties as required and participate as a full member of the Finance and Governance team


Person Specification: 

The successful candidate will have: 

 

  • Strong interpersonal and relationship management skills. 
  • Proven ability to handle sensitive and confidential information securely.
  • Excellent attention to detail and ability to work accurately with confidential information
  • Strong administrative and organisation skills
  • Ability to build trusted working relationships with senior stakeholders. 
  • High levels of professionalism, discretion and confidentiality. 
  • Strong problem-solving ability and attention to detail. 
  • Commitment to continuous improvement and governance best practice. 
  • Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a team. 
  • Flexibility and adaptability in a dynamic environment.


Essential Criteria:

In order to be eligible to apply for this role you must have / demonstrate in your application form the following:


  • A minimum of 3 years' relevant experience in a data protection compliance role is required 
  • Thorough knowledge and understanding of the GDPR core principles and data subject rights including knowledge of relevant legislation, demonstrated through work experience. 
  • Holder of a recognised privacy credential 
  • Practical experience processing, reviewing, managing and redacting documents for Data Subject Access Requests. 
  • Demonstrable experience building and maintaining effective relationships with internal and external stakeholders. 
  • Excellent Microsoft Office skills, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook.  
  • A professional qualification (min level 6 under the QQI framework) in a related discipline (Business, Law, Governance, Public Administration, Finance or a related discipline) 


Desirable Requirements:

 

  • Experience using compliance management databases. 
  • Experience assisting with or delivering basic data protection training to staff. 
  • Experience supporting governance and compliance activities through work experience 


Key Competencies


  • Decision Making
  • Managing Relationships
  • Communicating Effectively
  • Planning and Managing Work


Office Location and Blended Working:

We do not ask for addresses as part of the application process, however it is the responsibility of the candidate to acknowledge the base location of the role. The successful candidate must regularly work from and attend the base office location of the role.

 

Please note: Remote working from outside the State is not permitted other than in exceptional circumstances. As this role is within the Irish public service, the post-holder must carry out a minimum of 80% of their working time within the State (Republic of Ireland). Candidates who reside in Northern Ireland must be able to meet this requirement.

 

  • This role requires travel, with attendance at a number of national and regional locations / sites on an annual basis.


 

Selection Process: 

Shortlisting will be based on applications and the selection process may involve two competency based interviews. A panel of successful candidates may be formed following the selection process.

 

Interview Attendance Requirement: 

Candidates must be available to attend an in-person interview at the location and date specified by Fáilte Ireland. Please note that the location of the interview may vary from the base location of the role.


Salary and Benefits

 

€58,528 – €83,697*.

*This role will be filled in line with Public Pay Policy at Point 1 of the relevant Salary Scale unless the successful candidate is appointed from an existing public sector role.


The Annual Leave allowance for this post is 27 days.

Job Purpose: 

 

Fáilte Ireland invites applications for the position of Officer, B2B Digital Marketing. The role sits within the B2B Digital Marketing team, B2B Strategy and Operations Division and is responsible for shaping and delivering a strategic, insight-led approach to digital engagement with Fáilte Ireland’s industry clients. It drives the evolution of our digital communications, channels and customer experience to make it easier for tourism businesses to access relevant information, supports and opportunities, with a particular focus on leading the Email Marketing Transformation Programme and using data, technology and customer insight to create more effective, personalised and measurable engagement. 

 

Job Description/ Key Areas of Responsability: 

  

  • Lead the delivery and implementation of the Email Marketing Transformation Programme, including new capabilities, processes, governance, customer journeys, segmentation and performance measurement frameworks. 
  • Develop and execute B2B digital marketing communications and campaigns across owned channels, using a user-centred and omnichannel approach. 
  • Use customer insight, segmentation, personalisation and performance data to improve engagement with industry clients and optimise campaign effectiveness. 
  • Work collaboratively across business, technology, data and content teams to integrate email marketing within Fáilte Ireland’s wider digital ecosystem. 
  • Support campaign reporting, insight generation, learnings and ROI analysis, and use findings to drive continuous improvement. 
  • Work with internal stakeholders and agency partners to plan, deliver and optimise B2B communications, campaigns and projects across Fáilte Ireland’s owned platforms, providing guidance on channel strategy, audience targeting and campaign effectiveness. 
  • Support the ongoing optimisation of failteireland.ie, including content planning, content creation and curation, website performance and engagement. 
  • Maintain email schedules and support accurate, timely delivery of content and channel changes. 
  • Monitor and report on owned-platform performance and other agreed KPIs. 
  • Contribute to media planning, B2B social media activity, and the development of industry activation assets and toolkits supporting consumer campaigns. 
  • Maintain a strong working knowledge of CRM, analytics and email marketing tools, including Google Analytics, Power BI and Microsoft Dynamics 365. 
  • Support team administration and financial management requirements and participate fully in the wider B2B Strategy and Operations team. 

 

 Resource Management

They will demonstrate sound judgement and flexibility, with the ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a collaborative team.   • Demonstrable experience delivering digital marketing campaigns or transformation projects involving digital agencies, technology teams and internal business stakeholders 
  • Strong practical knowledge of digital and email marketing, using data, customer insight and performance reporting to support segmentation, personalisation, testing, optimisation and decision-making 
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and experience using CRM, email marketing, web analytics or reporting platforms. 


Desirable Requirements:

Job Purpose: 

 

Fáilte Ireland invites applications for the position of Officer, Investment Services to help lead the organisation in the design and delivery of a comprehensive and diverse portfolio of investment grant schemes ensuring funding to tourism businesses is allocated for best tourism impact in order to drive growth in the tourism economy.   

This is an exciting opportunity to join a new, dynamic and innovative division responsible for directing Fáilte Ireland’s investment priorities and working across the organisation to realise change and impact. Reporting to the Manager, Investment Services, the successful candidate will have demonstrable experience in investment grant scheme design, execution and delivery.  

 

They will: 

 

  • Be able to operationalise investment grant services, adept in the delivering grant schemes and the development of process and procedural documenting and reporting.

  • Be highly organised and agile and show good judgement, attention to quality outcomes and critical thinking skills.

job.title: Officer, Investment Services (Full-time, Permanent)
job.description:
Key Details:

 

Location: Dublin, Sligo or Cork

Contract: Full-time, Permanent

Salary: €58,528 – €83,697 (starting at the first point of the scale)

Closing date: Wednesday, 28 October 2026 at 3pm


Application Form: Failte Ireland_Officer Investment Services_Application Form.docx


Job Purpose: 

 

Fáilte Ireland invites applications for the position of Officer, Investment Services to help lead the organisation in the design and delivery of a comprehensive and diverse portfolio of investment grant schemes ensuring funding to tourism businesses is allocated for best tourism impact in order to drive growth in the tourism economy.  

 

This is an exciting opportunity to join a new, dynamic and innovative division responsible for directing Fáilte Ireland’s investment priorities and working across the organisation to realise change and impact. Reporting to the Manager, Investment Services, the successful candidate will have demonstrable experience in: 

 

  • Service design and/or design thinking methodologies and practices, business process design and customer experience management 
  • Investment grant scheme execution and delivery or comparable client-facing programmes and services  


They will:


  • Be solutions focused, creative and curious, and work to ensure the organisation has the most customer-centric, easy and resource efficient services possible 
  • Demonstrate a strong focus on service & client impact measurement, service quality, service process & procedure documenting and reporting 
  • Be highly organised and agile and show good judgement, strategic planning and critical thinking skills
  • Support colleagues in operationalising investment grant services through the development of procedural and training documentation and effective communications content 
  • Assess and evaluate investment grant applications developing robust recommendations for considerations and decision  



Job Description/ Key Areas of Responsability: 

  

The Investment Services Officer will be responsible for working with management and colleagues to deliver and continuously improve the end-to-end service process across a portfolio of tourism investment schemes, in a way that is easy for the client business (service-user) and effective and efficient for the organisation to deliver, while ensuring robust governance, clear measures/KPIs, impactful analysis and reporting. 


Innovative Service Improvement

The Investment Services Officer will identify lean, effective and innovative solutions for the organisation, using insights to identify opportunities across all parts of a service including systems, processes and the end-user experience. This will be achieved through: 

 

  • Insights gathering, workshops/consultations to improve organisational services provided.
  • Working across the end-to-end service journey from scheme initiation, through to close, working collaborative to improve areas such as client engagement, governance and reporting and supporting the development of a new grant management system.  
  • Collaborating with and effectively communicating with colleagues, service users and stakeholders to identify and drive opportunities, efficiencies and solutions to deliver better outcomes.   
  • Develop and share insights through appropriate report formats to inform better business decisions shape future investment decision
  • Conducting user testing as required
  • Documenting and managing solutions from inception to conclusion in multi-disciplinary teams, this might include mapping processes, insights, opportunities, barriers, risks, etc.
  • Effectively gather and interpret data (qualitative & quantitative) and codesign research insights into opportunities which create prospects for service improvements/new services.
  • Actively support Divisional colleagues in the development of a new Investment Grant Management system, translating functional requirements into system design requirements. 

 

Investment Scheme Operations

  • Scheme design and maintenance including guidelines, application forms, operational procedures and supporting documentation.
  • Undertake assessment and evaluation processes through information gathering, validation and analysis.
  • Prepare recommendation reports, briefings and presentations for management and relevant internal and external stakeholders. 
  • Support scheme launch and communications/content development activities.
  • Actively engage in continuous improvement, reflection and learning initiatives.
  • Carry out quality control activities.

 

Stakeholder Management and Collaboration

  • Engage and consult with internal business owners to capture business requirements as part of the initial scheme briefing, gathering insights as required.
  • Work collaboratively and communicate well with colleagues across the Investment Services Division to ensure seamless service delivery.
  • Build and maintain positive working relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
  • Contribute to cross-functional projects and organisational priorities.

 

Resource Management

  • Plan, organise and deliver assigned work activities to agreed timelines, quality standards and priorities and seeking guidance or escalation where required.
  • Assume line-management responsibility as required
  • Be flexible and open to evolving the role as the new team embeds and ways of working mature
  • Support effective use of resources by following agreed processes, maintaining accurate records and contributing to continuous improvement and learning in day-to-day delivery.

 

Governance & Reporting

  • Comply with all relevant organisational policies, procedures and governance requirements in the delivery of assigned work, escalating issues appropriately.
  • Monitor progress against assigned tasks, plans and timelines, highlighting risks, issues or delays to the relevant manager in a timely manner.
  • Prepare accurate updates, information, reports or analysis as required to support decision-making, planning and delivery within the area.
  • Ensure assigned programme, project or operational activity is delivered in line with Fáilte Ireland policy, public sector obligations and delegated authority.

 

Corporate Responsibility  

  • Build effective working relationships with colleagues, stakeholders and partners, communicating clearly and constructively to support collaborative delivery.
  • Model Fáilte Ireland’s corporate values, contribute positively to team and organisational culture, support change and improvement initiatives, and carry out any other duties as may be assigned from time to time.

 

Carry out other responsibilities as required and participate as a full member of the Investment Services team by supporting different work projects from time to time.


Person Specification: 

The successful candidate will have: 

 

  • Relevant experience in Service Design / design thinking and service process design/improvement in the area of grant services or similar client/customer facing services.
  • Service design / design thinking experience 
  • Strong interpersonal and written communication skills, proficient at both developing and delivering impactful presentations 
  • Demonstrate a client-focused approach, sound judgement and the ability and flexibility to work across multiple priorities



Essential Criteria:

In order to be eligible to apply for this role you must have / demonstrate in your application form the following:


  • Three years’ experience relevant experience in Service Design and the delivery or improvement of investment grant schemes or comparable client-facing operations
  • Experience documenting, reviewing or improving end-to-end business processes, workflows or service-user journeys.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including demonstrable experience in gathering, validating and interpreting information to support assessment, reporting and decision-making
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel, Word, Teams and PowerPoint
  • Experience in writing documentation including procedure & briefing documentation for approval. The candidate should be experienced in interpreting complex/technical information to produce content/documents that can be easily understood and communicated to various audiences  
  • A professional qualification (min level 6 under the QQI framework) in a related discipline


Desirable Requirements:

 

  • Experience of working in the area of public investment/grant schemes
  • Good understanding of the public sector investment landscape.
  • Strong skills in using process/co-creation and collaboration tools (e.g., Miro, Mural, etc)
  • Experience using investment management or grant management systems
  • Familiarity with the legislative and policy environment in which public sector investment grant schemes operate including public-sector governance, State Aid, procurement or public-spending requirements.
  • Good understanding of Irish tourism, destination development, regional economic development policies 
  • Externally service provider contract management experience
  • People management experience  


Key Competencies


  • Managing Relationships
  • Communicating Effectively
  • Planning and Managing Work
  • Embracing Innovation


Office Location and Blended Working:

We do not ask for addresses as part of the application process, however it is the responsibility of the candidate to acknowledge the base location of the role. The successful candidate must regularly work from and attend the base office location of the role.

 

Please note: Remote working from outside the State is not permitted other than in exceptional circumstances. As this role is within the Irish public service, the post-holder must carry out a minimum of 80% of their working time within the State (Republic of Ireland). Candidates who reside in Northern Ireland must be able to meet this requirement.

 

  • This role requires travel, with attendance at a number of national and regional locations / sites on an annual basis.
  •  The flexibility to travel domestically, and on occasion internationally, is an element of this role.

 

Selection Process: 

Shortlisting will be based on applications and the selection process may involve two competency based interviews. A panel of successful candidates may be formed following the selection process.

 

Interview Attendance Requirement: 

Candidates must be available to attend an in-person interview at the location and date specified by Fáilte Ireland. Please note that the location of the interview may vary from the base location of the role.


Salary and Benefits

 

€58,528 – €83,697*.

*This role will be filled in line with Public Pay Policy at Point 1 of the relevant Salary Scale unless the successful candidate is appointed from an existing public sector role.


The Annual Leave allowance for this post is 27 days.


Further details on the benefits on offer can be found in the Why Work with Fáilte Ireland? | Fáilte Ireland · Failte Ireland


How to Apply


Conscia will be managing all aspects of the recruitment process on behalf of Fáilte Ireland

Late applications will be ineligible for consideration. Therefore, it is your responsibility to ensure that you have allowed sufficient time for transmission of your application.

job.title: Lecturer / Programme Director, Leadership and Management (Maternity Leave cover)
job.description:
Title: Lecturer / Programme Director, Leadership and Management

 

Grade: IPA Grade 3

 

Reports to: Dean of Whitaker School of Government and Management

 

Duration: Specified Purpose Contract (envisaged up to December 2027)


Salary: Starting salary €69,375 per annum rising to €106,749 (14-point salary scale, the top 2 points are long service increments)


Closing date: 1pm (Irish time) on Wednesday 28th October

About the IPA


The Institute of Public Administration exists to support a capable, confident and effective Public Service in Ireland. Our purpose is to strengthen the capability and leadership required to meet complex demands, make sound decisions and contribute to better public services for the people of Ireland. We do this through learning and leadership development that is evidence‑based, practice‑led and focused on application at a whole-of-government level.

As a trusted, government-supported institution, we provide an open and inclusive space for learning, reflection and exchange across the Public Service. We bring people together across organisational and sectoral boundaries to strengthen shared understanding, professional standards and continuous improvement.


About the Role

The Whitaker School is seeking to appoint a Lecturer/Programme Director to contribute to its teaching, programme development and academic activities in the broad areas of leadership and management. The successful candidate will combine teaching with responsibility for the effective academic direction and coordination of designated programmes and will contribute to the ongoing development of the School's academic portfolio. 

 

The role provides an opportunity to work across teaching and learning, programme development, academic quality, research and practitioner scholarship, and engagement with public service organisations. The successful candidate will be expected to bring contemporary thinking and evidence into their teaching, contribute positively to the intellectual life of the School, and support the development of programmes that respond to evolving public service needs. 

 

Working as part of a multidisciplinary academic team, the Lecturer/Programme Director will have opportunities to develop their own areas of expertise and scholarship while contributing to the wider mission and development of the Whitaker School and the IPA.


Key Responsibilities

Teaching 

  • To lecture in leadership and management subjects such as leadership, management development, change management, innovation, design thinking and project management. Lecturing will take place in-person and on-line, on the Institute’s daytime, evening and weekend undergraduate, postgraduate and international programmes. 
  • To design courses and programmes in subjects such as leadership, management development, change management, innovation, design thinking and project management.  
  • To develop new and existing course material, including IPA bespoke course texts and learning materials, and using new learning technology and delivery mechanisms as required. 
  • To set and correct examinations and assignments, actively engage with external examiners and assist with the administration of examinations. 
  • To supervise and correct postgraduate assignments and dissertations up to and including, level 10 professional doctorate.  
  • To provide feedback on submitted project work both orally and in writing when required. 
  • To interact with colleagues, both internal and external, in relation to assessment moderation. 
  • To address student feedback and queries that may arise. 
  • To undertake the teaching duties of the role in accordance with the requirements of the IPA’s Quality Assurance arrangements. 
  • To liaise with library regarding reading material and booklists etc. 

  

Programme Development 

  • To assist in the development of existing programmes and new programmes, including drafting submission documents, liaising with the validating bodies, promoting, implementing and reviewing programmes. 

 

Research

  • To develop and maintain expertise in relevant subject areas. 
  • To develop research links with other colleagues and institutions 
  • To carry out scholarly and/or public service research relevant to IPA’s activities including regular publications and presentations. 

 

Programme Direction and other Administrative Duties

  • To co-ordinate the teaching and assessment duties of relevant contributing and associate lecturers; to liaise with fellow lecturers, editorial manager and Dean/Registrar’s Office on programme governance and administration. 
  • To co-ordinate, with lecturing colleagues, the scheduling, content and communication for classes, seminars and associated virtual learning platforms.  
  • To contribute to the development and implementation of Quality Assurance processes and mechanisms, both at programme and School level, including programmatic reviews, evaluation and student and stakeholder engagement. 
  • To participate in faculty meetings; lead faculty working groups conducting educational research and other projects; and contribute to conferrings, other internal and external meetings and the annual cycle of programme promotion and marketing. 
  • To undertake such other duties as may be assigned from time to time. 

 

Essential Criteria


  • A postgraduate qualification at Master’s level or higher in management, leadership, public administration, business or a closely related field
  • Proficiency in commonly used digital presentation, communication and learning tools, including Microsoft Office/365 or equivalent
  • Relevant lecturing experience in leadership, management or a related subject area within higher education, professional education or adult learning
  • Strong organisational and administrative skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and deadlines
  • Strong analytical and written communication skills
  • Effective communication and interpersonal skills



Desirable Criteria

  • A PhD or comparable Level 10 qualification in a relevant field
  • Demonstrable experience of designing or developing learning content, programmes or assessment materials
  • Demonstrable experience of coordinating or administering an academic, professional development or learning programme
  • Experience of teaching at both undergraduate and postgraduate level
  • Experience of lecturing, researching or delivering learning within a public service or wider public sector environment
  • Experience of supervising dissertations or research projects at Master’s level or above
  • Demonstrated track record of research, publication, conference presentation or other relevant scholarly activity

 

Full details of essential and desirable criteria, along with additional information, can be found in the candidate booklet.


How to Apply:

 

Conscia will be managing all aspects of the recruitment process on behalf of The IPA. Applications should be made online through https://consciatalent.com/IPA and must include:


• an up-to-date CV; and

• a cover letter clearly demonstrating how your qualifications, knowledge and experience meet the essential criteria set out on page 7 of the Candidate Booklet, and, where applicable, any desirable criteria you also meet.


Download Candidate Booklet here.pdf

 

Your application must be submitted on the Conscia website not later than 1pm (Irish time) on Wednesday 28th October.

 

If you do not receive an acknowledgement of receipt of your application within 24 hours of applying, please email: ipa@consciatalent.com

job.title: Electrification Support Engineer
job.description:
Electrification Support Engineer


An exciting opportunity to play a key role in supporting Dublin Bus’s transition to an electric fleet.


We’re looking for an experienced EV/EV Charging Engineer to ensure the charging infrastructure, chargers, vehicles and Charge Management System are operating reliably and efficiently across Dublin Bus depots.


What you’ll be doing:

• Monitor and troubleshoot EV charging systems and infrastructure

• Act as the technical point of contact for suppliers, contractors and service providers

• Manage incidents, root-cause analysis and technical changes through to resolution

• Support depot teams with technical guidance and training

• Help develop processes and support future phases of fleet electrification


What we’re looking for:

• Engineering qualification or relevant technical/trade background

• Strong experience with EV charging / electrification

• Knowledge of OCPP, ISO 15118 and/or VDV protocols

• Experience in technical support, service delivery or operational engineering

• A genuine interest in EV technology and fleet electrification


Location: Dublin

﻿

This is a great opportunity for someone who wants to be directly involved in keeping a growing electric bus fleet operational and supporting the next stage of Dublin’s transport electrification.

job.title: Electrical Engineer
job.description:
About IN2 

Formed in 2002, IN2 is a progressive engineering consultancy operating across Ireland, the UK, and Europe, dedicated to creating better spaces for people. With over 100 experts across six locations, our team of engineers, technicians, and consultants collaborate closely with clients and partners to deliver innovative, sustainable, and energy-efficient building solutions across a wide range of sectors—from concept and design through to handover and beyond. 

For over 20 years, we have maintained a people-centric culture that encourages growth, innovation, and adaptability. Our award-winning MEP projects, combined with recognition as a ‘Great Place to Work’, reflect our commitment to quality, sustainability, and a supportive, inclusive work environment where individuals can thrive. 

At IN2, joining our team means being part of a collaborative, high-performing, and forward-thinking organisation, where your contribution makes a real impact—and where career opportunities grow alongside our business. 

 

Working Hours  

We operate a 37.5-hour working week designed to support work-life balance. We offer flexible start and finish times between 8am and 6pm, provided that core hours of 10am to 4pm are covered for team collaboration and meetings.  

 

About The Role 

We are seeking an experienced Electrical Engineer to join our growing Athlone team. This is a permanent position offering an excellent package for the right candidate.  You’ll play a key role in project delivery and receive mentorship from senior engineers to support your career development. 


What you will do 

Athlone offers the chance to do career-defining work without long commutes or city pressure. You will be trusted, supported, and encouraged to shape how things are done locally, with full backing from the wider IN2 team.  As a Senior Electrical Engineer at our Athlone Office, you will:   

  • Assist senior engineers with project management, on-site inspections, technical surveys, and design team meetings 
  • Play an active role in project delivery from concept through to completion 
  • Support the management team in client relationships, budgeting, and reporting 
  • Contribute to mentoring junior staff, reviewing design work, and providing guidance 
  • Collaborate with senior engineers for ongoing mentorship and growth 


Your Experience 

To be considered for this role, you should have:  


Essential 

  • Degree in Building Services Engineering or Electrical Engineering 
  • Minimum of 4 years’ experience in electrical design, ideally within a consultancy environment 
  • Passion for career progression and aspiration to achieve Chartered status (if not already obtained) 


Why You’ll Love Being Part of the Team 

At IN2, we’ve traded the stuffy corporate ladder for a flat hierarchy and a culture where your voice actually matters. We’re a diverse, collaborative team that believes the best ideas can come from anyone, anywhere. 

  • Global Impact, Local Feel: You’ll get to work on game-changing projects across different countries, supported by our specialist BIM, Sustainability, and Building Physics teams. 
  • Constant Growth: Through IN2 Talks, cross-office collaboration, and a culture of knowledge sharing, you’re always learning something new. 
  • Your Best Self: We prioritise a genuine work-life balance with flexible hours and support for personal circumstances. We’re big on open communication and ensuring our workplace is a bias-free zone where you can truly be yourself. 


What’s In It For You? 

We’ve put together a package that looks after your wallet, your career, and your wellbeing. 


The Essentials 

  • Competitive Pay & Bonuses: A salary that reflects your worth, plus an annual bonus and pension contributions. 
  • Annual Leave: 22 days of annual leave, scaling up to 27 days as you grow with us (plus all those bank holidays!). 
  • Flexible Hours: Work-life balance isn't just a buzzword here—we offer a 37.5-hour working week with flexible hours (8am–6pm), to suit your lifestyle! 


Career Progression 

  • Personal Roadmap: You’ll have a dedicated Personal Development Plan and mentoring from our senior leaders. 
  • The IN2 Academy: Access to our internal academy, CPD support, and expert assistance in advancing your career,  

 

Health & Wellbeing 

  • Mind & Body: Access to our Employee Assistance Program, annual health checks, and various fitness initiatives. 
  • Commute Greener: Take advantage of our Cycle to Work scheme to keep active on your way to the office. 


Social & Community 

  • Legendary Events: From our famous Christmas party weekend to Employee Appreciation Day and regular staff social events. 
  • Giving Back: Get involved with our team-led charity initiatives. 
  • International Reach: opportunities to work across IN2 offices in London, Dublin, Berlin, Belfast, Athlone, and Madrid 


Eligibility: Due to regulatory requirements, this role is open to candidates with permanent residency or unrestricted right to work in Ireland only. Applications requiring visa sponsorship cannot be considered.

job.title: Senior Electrical Engineer
job.description:
Senior Electrical Engineer

Own the outcome. Not just the design.

Senior Engineers at IN2 lead from the front, responsible for decisions, direction, and delivery across multiple high-value projects.


The Role

As a Senior Electrical Engineer at IN2, you will take ownership of electrical design delivery across major projects, helping shape technical

direction, maintain quality, and build trusted relationships with clients and project teams. This is a hands-on role for someone who can

lead confidently, think strategically, and deliver to a high standard.


What You'll Do

  • Lead electrical design across multiple high-value projects
  • Oversee technical delivery and quality standards
  • Act as a key client contact and build long-term relationships
  • Coordinate with internal teams and external stakeholders
  • Mentor and support junior engineers
  • Contribute to innovation and sustainability strategies



What You'll Bring

  • Degree in Electrical or Building Services Engineering
  • 6+ years' experience in electrical design
  • Strong technical knowledge of building systems and standards
  • Experience leading projects and managing clients
  • Chartered or working towards Chartership desirable
  • Strong leadership and communication skills



What You'll Get 

This isn't built around perks. It's built around how high-performing engineers actually want to work. Real ownership, real progression,

and a culture that trusts you to deliver.


The Essentials

  • Competitive salary, bonus and pension that reflect your impact
  • 22 to 27 days annual leave, plus bank holidays
  • Flexible working across a 37.5 hour week: early start or later start? you decide

Career Progression

  • A clear path forward, with responsibility increasing as you prove it
  • Direct exposure to senior leaders, not layers of hierarchy
  • IN2 Academy, CPD support and chartership guidance
  • Fully paid professional fees

Health and Wellbeing

  • Employee Assistance Programme and annual health checks
  • Wellbeing and fitness initiatives that support you long term
  • Cycle to Work scheme to make the everyday easier

Social and Community

  • Genuinely strong team culture, built through regular events and shared wins
  • Employee-led charity initiatives with real involvement
  • Offices in Dublin, London, Berlin, Belfast, Athlone and Madrid



Why IN2?

Across every role, electrical, mechanical, or BIM, the IN2 difference is the same: you're expected to think, lead, and shape outcomes, not just execute instructions. Here's what sets us apart.

Ownership from Day One

Whether you're an Engineer or a Senior, you'll have real accountability and decision-making authority. No waiting for permission. No layers of sign-off slowing you down.

Progression Based on Ability

Faster progression based on what you deliver, not how long you've been in the seat. A clear pathway from Engineer to Senior, Associate, and beyond.

Innovation Time

Dedicated time to develop new ideas, explore emerging technologies, and contribute to sustainability strategies: built into how we work, not bolted on.

High-Performance, Low-Ego Culture

A team that challenges each other, supports each other, and wins together. No hierarchy for hierarchy's sake. Just talented people doing exceptional work.

Complex, High-Profile Projects

Exposure to design-led, high-impact developments that push the boundaries of what building services engineering can achieve.

Global Reach

Work across offices in Dublin, London, Berlin, Belfast, Athlone, and Madrid- a genuinely international practice with a collaborative, connected culture.


Ready to own the outcome? Join a team that expects more and gives more in return.

job.title: Cyber Underwriter
job.description:
Does it ever feel like you’re underwriting with one hand tied behind your back? Tired of the struggles and inefficiencies associated with legacy systems and processes? Spending too much of your time and energy navigating corporate politics? All leaving your efforts to innovate and deliver underwriting excellence languishing?

At Ledgebrook, we believe a career in underwriting can be so much more. You bring the passion and entrepreneurial spirit; we’ll provide the platform to unleash the very best of your talents and skills. Together, we’ll celebrate and reward success! Are you intrigued? Then read on and apply now to advance your career at Ledgebrook.

About the Role

We are seeking experienced Cyber Liability underwriting talent to join our growing team whose mission is focused on building a profitable book of cyber liability business. Our vision is to deliver market relevant solutions to our key wholesale trading partners in a more frictionless environment that places an emphasis on efficiencies and quality to meet or exceed our broker’s overall needs in a risk differentiated manner. If you possess an entrepreneurial passion that includes a proven track history of delivering underwriting excellence and are seeking an opportunity to break out of the traditional insurance company mould, we’re looking for you!

As a member of the Cyber team, you will regularly interact with our wholesale trading partners over the phone, virtually and in-person to drive submission flow and convert on the best opportunities quoted. We are looking for disciplined underwriting candidates that possess a strong overall cyber liability background with experience underwriting risks of all industries and sizes.

We are flexible with both a candidate’s experience level and physical work location. The actual position title (Underwriter, Senior UW, AVP, etc.) will be dependent on a candidate’s specific experience and qualifications. We currently operate in a fully remote work environment, so we’re more focused on your experience and cultural fit than where you physically sit!

About You

Here at Ledgebrook we’re passionate about creating a team that thrives on continuous learning and shares our excitement about building a company from the ground up. We’re looking for people to join us with:

●     A passion for delivering world-class customer service to our internal and external customers

●     Intellectual curiosity and a strong desire for innovation, rather than following the status quo

●     A hunger for continuous learning and opportunities to grow

●     Agile prioritization skills coupled with a keen sense of urgency - we balance getting it right with getting it done right now

●     A strong drive and desire to win together as a high-performing team

●     A moral compass to "do the right thing, period." We have zero tolerance for toxic behaviors

●     An eagerness to actively participate and connect with the whole team, across remote locations

●     An honest, transparent communication style

●     A proactive, solution-oriented mindset. We don’t look for blame, we look for the solution

As a future Cyber Liability Underwriter, your experience and qualifications must include:

●     2+ years experience as a cyber underwriter

●     Experience working in the Cyber E&S market; Tech E&O experience is a plus

●     Ability to work as a team player or independently in a fast-paced work environment

●     Deep wholesale broker trading relationships

●     Effective communication skills to articulate our appetite and develop wholesale broker relationships

●     Understanding of pricing and risk selection criteria to achieve underwriting profit

●     Advanced understanding of data analysis and execution of portfolio management objectives

●     Intellectual curiosity, problem solving skills, and a sense of urgency

●     Responsive, customer service focused mindset and behaviors

●     Ability to make timely decisions with appropriate information and consultation

●     A strong entrepreneurial drive and desire to build and win together as a high performing team

●     Ability to travel to meet with assigned brokers or with the broader team to participate in industry conference or events
